It covers source-backed Table 5 successful-void file appends for the wrappers enumerated by this contract, plus the selected public federation-management service-report interaction vector for synchronization registration/confirmation/achievement. Local Delete Object Instance adds type-37 ObjectInstanceHandle as quoted handle.toString() text after its accepted §6.18 local-forget transition, with no separate callback boundary. Publish Object Class Attributes adds type-36 ObjectClassHandle as quoted handle.toString() text and type-1 AttributeHandleSet as a bracketed array of quoted AttributeHandle::toString() elements after its accepted §5.2 declaration transition, before separately queued declaration advisories and ownership-assumption work. Unpublish Object Class Attributes adds the same type-36/type-1 forms after its accepted §5.3 teardown and synchronous ownership cleanup, before separately queued declaration advisories. Subscribe Object Class Attributes adds type-36 ObjectClassHandle and type-1 AttributeHandleSet forms, type-6 Boolean Optional passive subscription indicator as the inverse of the public C++ active selector, and either type-53 String Optional update rate designator or type-34 Null when the default rate is selected. Its accepted §5.8 record precedes separately queued declaration, scope, relevance, and discovery callbacks; RL-080 records the Lab's cross-page update-rate candidate ownership mismatch. Unsubscribe Object Class Attributes adds type-36 ObjectClassHandle and type-1 AttributeHandleSet for the official C++ attribute-set overload. The official whole-class overload retains the required optional-set slot as type-34 Null rather than serializing a supplied-empty set. Both accepted §5.9 records precede separately queued declaration, scope, and relevance callbacks; the Lab assigns their coalesced source candidates to §5.9.4 rather than §5.9 itself (RL-078). Publish Interaction Class adds type-27 InteractionClassHandle as quoted handle.toString() text after its accepted §5.4 declaration transition, before any separately queued declaration advisories. Subscribe Interaction Class adds type-27 InteractionClassHandle and type-6 Boolean Optional passive subscription indicator after its accepted §5.10 declaration transition, before any separately queued declaration advisories. The public C++ active selector is inverted to the standards-facing passive indicator, and its text uses §11.5.1 lowercase true/false rather than the uppercase Table 5 example (RL-079). Unpublish Interaction Class adds the same type-27 form after its accepted §5.5 declaration transition, also before separately queued declaration advisories. Unsubscribe Interaction Class adds the same type-27 form after its accepted §5.11 ordinary-unsubscription invocation, again before separately queued declaration advisories. Query Attribute Transportation Type adds type-37 ObjectInstanceHandle and type-0 AttributeHandle as quoted handle.toString() values when its query plan is accepted, before its later Report Attribute Transportation Type callback. Query Attribute Ownership adds type-37 ObjectInstanceHandle and type-1 AttributeHandleSet as quoted handle.toString() text and a bracketed array of quoted AttributeHandle::toString() elements at the accepted-query boundary, before its later ownership-result callbacks. Unconditional Attribute Ownership Divestiture adds those type-37/type-1 forms and a Binary Data user tag at accepted §7.2 invocation, before any later §7.4 ownership-assumption callback. Its file text follows Table 5's literal type 63, kept separate from a future encoded MOM-interaction path because the companion standard MIM calls UserSuppliedTag type 60 (RL-077). Query Interaction Transportation Type adds type-15 FederateHandle and type-27 InteractionClassHandle as quoted handle.toString() values at the same accepted-query boundary, before its later Report Interaction Transportation Type callback. Change Default Attribute Transportation Type proves ObjectClassHandle type 36 and TransportationTypeHandle type 59 as quoted handle.toString() values, with AttributeHandleSet type 1 as a bracketed array of quoted AttributeHandle::toString() elements, after an accepted prospective class-default invocation. Request Federation Save preserves its required type-53 Federation save label and the optional timestamp's public-overload distinction: omitted is type-34 Null, supplied is type-31 LogicalTime using the private clone's quoted time.toString() value. Both admitted §4.19 records precede separately queued Initiate Federate Save work. Request Federation Restore adds its one type-53 Federation save label after the request returns normally and before its later positive or negative confirmation callback; a missing snapshot or membership mismatch is a confirmation outcome, not a substitute failed-service record. Federate Restore Complete maps both C++ selector calls to one type-6 Federate restore-success indicator record before the corresponding Federation Restored or Federation Not Restored callback. The selected RTI-initiated Federate Resigned and Connection Lost paths reserve their final serials before member removal, append their distinct type-53 reason or fault strings, and then queue their separate callbacks. The per-joined-federate serial sequence remains live audit state across application snapshot restore, so a durable file never reuses a previously written serial. The public MOM HLAreportServiceFile attribute is separately covered through the standard Java reflection route, including its configured filesystem value and reliable delivery. The previously admitted successful-void wrappers use the table's explicit [null] return form; the later lookup and Register Object Instance entries use their selected type-specific return forms. The two self-selecting switches remain deferred because report eligibility/sink ordering across their own state transition is unresolved (RL-066). This does not prove generic return values, failures, received interactions beyond the selected callback-report boundary, Requirements Lab validation, or conformance. Table 5 lacks row-level requirement candidates and drops rotated continuation rows from its structured table export (RL-067/RL-076), while the general ReturnArgument mapping and RTI-created callback producer identity remain unresolved (RL-042/RL-043); these are source-level traceability records only.
